read.sections.0.heading.source: Remembering is a choice made in the present
read.sections.0.heading.back: Remembering is a choice made in the present

read.sections.0.text.source:
A monument is made at a particular time to remember something. Its subject may belong to a much earlier period. So studying it involves two historical questions. What is being remembered? And why did later people choose to remember it in this form? The artist, the people who commissioned it, its place and its audience all shape that public account.

In the 1880s, the French town of Calais commissioned a monument from Auguste Rodin. It would commemorate, or publicly remember, citizens linked with the Hundred Years' War. Rodin drew on the medieval writer Jean Froissart's account of the siege of 1347. In that account, six leading citizens offered themselves to England's King Edward III in exchange for the town's protection. Rodin's sculpture shows them setting out, when their fate was uncertain. It is a nineteenth-century interpretation of a medieval story, not an eyewitness record.
read.sections.0.text.back:
A monument is made at a particular time to remember something. Its subject may come from a much earlier time. So studying it involves two history questions. What is being remembered? And why did people later choose to remember it in this form? Its artist, the people who ordered it, its place and its audience all shape that public account.

In the 1880s, the town of Calais in France ordered a monument from Auguste Rodin. The monument would commemorate, or remember in public, citizens of the town connected with the Hundred Years' War. Rodin used the account by the Middle Ages writer Jean Froissart of the siege of 1347. In that account, six leading citizens gave themselves up to King Edward III of England in exchange for protection for their town. Rodin's statue shows them as they set off, when their fate was not yet certain. The statue is a 19th-century interpretation of a Middle Ages story, not an eyewitness record.
read.sections.0.text.note: "commemorate" is "memperingati" (glossary form of "peringatan"). The six citizens "menyerahkan diri" (gave themselves up), kept brief as the sensitive note asks.

read.sections.0.simpler.source:
A monument helps people remember. It may be about a much earlier time. So we ask two questions. What is remembered? And why did later people remember it this way? The artist, the people who paid, the place and the viewers all matter.

In the 1880s, the town of Calais in France asked Rodin for a monument. It would commemorate some of its people from a long war. To commemorate means to remember in public. Rodin used a story by Jean Froissart, a writer from the Middle Ages. In 1347, an army surrounded Calais. Six leading men offered themselves to England's king, Edward III. In return, he would keep the town safe. Rodin shows the men as they leave, not knowing what will happen. He made it more than 500 years later.
read.sections.0.simpler.back:
A monument helps people remember. A monument can be about a much earlier time. So we ask two things. What is remembered? And why did people later remember it in this way? Its artist, the people who paid, its place and its audience all matter.

In the 1880s, the town of Calais in France asked Rodin to make a monument. The monument would commemorate some of its citizens from a long war. To commemorate means to remember together in public. Rodin used a story by Jean Froissart, a writer from the Middle Ages. In 1347, an army surrounded Calais. Six leading men of the town gave themselves up to the English king, Edward III. In return, the king would keep the town safe. Rodin shows them as they leave, not knowing what will happen. He made it more than 500 years later.

read.sections.1.text.source:
The group has six figures, each with a different gesture and expression. Rodin placed them all on one level instead of raising one above the others. Plain clothes and vulnerable poses make the monument very different from a statue of a victorious ruler on horseback. Here, civic courage, the courage of a town's citizens, appears as people facing a hard choice together. Each one responds in his own way.

The town council had first planned a monument to Eustache de Saint-Pierre, the best-known citizen in the group. By including all six, Rodin shifted attention toward a shared action. This was a choice about public memory as well as composition. Deciding whom to show helped define the story the town would remember in public.

A separate figure, Jean d'Aire, helps us study those decisions. The National Gallery of Art's version shows a clothed man standing firmly and holding a large key. His posture and hands give the figure weight. A whole group and a single study offer different views of the same larger project. Their size and the way they are displayed also affect how an audience meets them.
read.sections.1.text.back:
The group has six figures, each with a different body movement and facial expression. Rodin placed them all at one height, instead of raising one person above the others. Simple clothes and fragile poses make this monument very different from a statue of a ruler who won, on a horse. Here, civic courage, that is, the courage of the citizens of a town, appears as people facing a hard choice together. Each one responds in his own way.

The town council at first planned a monument to Eustache de Saint-Pierre, the best-known citizen in the group. By including all six, Rodin turned attention to a shared action. This was a choice about public memory as well as about composition. Deciding who would be shown helped decide the story the town would remember in public.

A separate figure, Jean d'Aire, helps us study those decisions. The National Gallery of Art's version shows a clothed man who stands upright and holds a large key. His posture and his hands make the figure feel weighty. One whole group and one single study give different views of the same big project. Their size and the way the two are displayed also affect how the audience meets them.
read.sections.1.text.note: "civic" is "kewargaan" (to do with citizens), explained in the text. "keberanian warga" alone would be easier; reviewers decide.

read.sections.1.simpler.source:
The monument has six men. Each one moves and looks in a different way. Rodin put them all on one level. They wear plain clothes. Their poses look weak, not proud. They are not like a king on a horse. It shows civic courage. Civic means about a town and its people. Here, courage means facing a hard choice together. But each man reacts in his own way.

At first, the town wanted a monument to one man, Eustache de Saint-Pierre. He was the best known of the six. Rodin showed all six instead. So the monument is about a shared act. Choosing whom to show shaped the story the town remembers.

Rodin also made a single figure, Jean d'Aire. A man stands firmly and holds a large key. His body and hands look strong. Their size and how they are shown change how we see them.
read.sections.1.simpler.back:
The monument has six men. Each one moves and looks in a different way. Rodin placed them all at the same height. Their clothes are simple. Their poses look weak, not proud. They are not like a king on a horse. This monument shows civic courage. Civic means about a town and its citizens. Here, being brave means facing a hard choice together. But each man responds in his own way.

At first, the town wanted a monument to one man, Eustache de Saint-Pierre. He was the best known of the six. Rodin showed all six instead. So this monument is about a shared action. Choosing who to show shaped the story the town remembers.

Rodin also made one figure on its own, Jean d'Aire. A man stands upright and holds a large key. His body and hands look strong. The size and the way a statue is displayed change the way we see it.

read.sections.2.heading.source: An artist's travels and a bronze's dates
read.sections.2.heading.back: An artist's travels and the dates of a bronze

read.sections.2.text.source:
Rodin's career also crossed borders. He grew up in a working-class district of Paris and trained in the decorative arts. After the Franco-Prussian War of 1870–71 disrupted work, he continued his career in Belgium. A later journey to Italy deepened his interest in Michelangelo's sculpture. Calling Rodin a French artist names an important connection. But his skills developed through particular schools, jobs and travel. Artistic culture was shaped by movement as well as by local institutions.

Dates need particular care with sculpture. A model can be made first, and a bronze cast, an object formed in a mould, can be produced much later. The Met's group was modelled in 1884–95 but cast in 1985. The National Gallery of Art's smaller Jean d'Aire was modelled in 1884–89 and probably cast in 1895. Neither is a bronze made at the time of the medieval event, and each museum object is a separate cast.
read.sections.2.text.back:
Rodin's career also crossed national borders. He grew up in a working-class district of Paris and studied decorative art. After the Franco-Prussian War of 1870–71 disrupted his work, he continued his career in Belgium. A journey to Italy later deepened his interest in Michelangelo's statues. Calling Rodin a French artist does name an important connection. But his skills developed through particular schools, jobs and travel. Art culture was shaped by people moving, as well as by local institutions.

Dates need careful attention with sculpture. A model can be made first, and a bronze cast, that is, an object formed in a mould, can be made much later. The Met's group of statues had its model made in 1884–95, but was cast in 1985. The National Gallery of Art's smaller Jean d'Aire had its model made in 1884–89 and was most likely cast in 1895. None of them is a bronze made at the time of that Middle Ages event, and each museum object is a separate cast.
read.sections.2.text.note: "cast" is "hasil cor" (glossary word "cor", form "dicor"). "probably" is "kemungkinan besar" throughout.

read.sections.2.simpler.source:
Rodin's life also crossed borders. He grew up in a part of Paris where working people lived. He learned to make decorations. A war in 1870 and 1871 stopped much of the work, so he worked in Belgium. Later, in Italy, he studied Michelangelo's sculpture. Rodin was French. But his skills came from schools, jobs and travel.

Dates need care with sculpture. First an artist makes a model. Then a bronze cast is made, maybe much later. A cast is made by pouring metal into a mould. The Met's group is from a model made in 1884–95. But it was cast in 1985. The smaller Jean d'Aire is from a model made in 1884–89. It was probably cast in 1895. Neither was made in 1347. Each one is a separate cast.
read.sections.2.simpler.back:
Rodin's life also crossed national borders. He grew up in a part of Paris where workers lived. He learned to make decorations. A war in 1870 and 1871 stopped a lot of work, so he worked in Belgium. Later, in Italy, he studied Michelangelo's statues. Rodin was French. But his skills came from schools, jobs and travel.

Dates need care with sculpture. First the artist makes a model. Then a bronze cast is made, maybe much later. A cast is made by pouring metal into a mould. The Met's group of statues comes from a model made in 1884–95. But the statue was cast in 1985. The smaller Jean d'Aire comes from a model made in 1884–89. That statue was most likely cast in 1895. None of them was made in 1347. Each is a separate cast.

write.example.source: Rodin chose to show six citizens on the same level, in plain clothes. Each one has a different gesture, and none of them stands above the others. The history tells us that the town council first wanted a monument to just one man, Eustache de Saint-Pierre. So the monument shows courage as something people share. Each man faces the same hard choice in his own way.
write.example.back: Rodin chose to show six citizens at the same height, in simple clothes. Each one has a different body movement, and none stands higher than the others. Its history tells us that the town council at first wanted a monument to only one man, Eustache de Saint-Pierre. So this monument shows courage as something held in common. Each man faces the same hard choice in his own way.

sensitiveNotes.0.source: The siege story turns on six citizens offering their lives to save their town, during a war. Keep the account brief and non-graphic, and don't ask for any reenactment or role-play of the threatened people. The Franco-Prussian War is named only as the reason Rodin moved to Belgium for work.
sensitiveNotes.0.back: This siege story centres on six citizens offering their lives to save their town, in wartime. Tell it briefly and without violent detail, and don't ask learners to act out or role-play the people who were threatened. The Franco-Prussian War is named only as the reason Rodin moved to Belgium for work.

educatorNotes.0.source: An old-looking monument is not necessarily from the time of the event it shows. Keep three dates apart: the siege (1347), the model (1884–95, or 1884–89 for Jean d'Aire) and each bronze's casting date (1985 for The Met's group, probably 1895 for the National Gallery of Art's figure).
educatorNotes.0.back: A monument that looks old is not necessarily from the time of the event it shows. Keep three dates apart: the siege (1347), the model (1884–95, or 1884–89 for Jean d'Aire) and each bronze's casting date (1985 for The Met's group, most likely 1895 for the National Gallery of Art's figure).

educatorNotes.1.source: Answer points for Write: a group of citizens on one level, varied gestures, vulnerability alongside courage; a town commission in the nineteenth century commemorating a much earlier event, and the council's first plan for Eustache de Saint-Pierre alone. Accept other supported readings; don't require a single definition of heroism.
educatorNotes.1.back: Answer points for Write: a group of citizens at one height, varied body movements, fragility alongside courage; a town's commission in the 19th century to commemorate a much earlier event, and the council's first plan for Eustache de Saint-Pierre alone. Accept other readings supported by evidence; don't require one definition of heroism.

educatorNotes.2.source: The Froissart-based story, the group composition and the commission come from The Met's educator resource on The Burghers of Calais (PDF, printed pages 11–12 and 16). Its chronology separates the council's decision in 1884 from Rodin's selection in 1885; the reading says "in the 1880s". The Hirshhorn's account confirms the civic commission; its photographs are not open for reuse.
